title: Take a job offer before the benefits details arrive?
summary: An uncertain decision page: what you can safely accept now, what to condition, and what to wait for before the benefits packet lands.

blocks.title: You can lean yes — you should not pretend the packet does not matter
blocks.body: Base pay and start date are arriving without medical, retirement match, PTO, or equity paperwork. This page separates what is safe to signal from what is reckless to finalize.

columns.name: Signal interest / soft accept
columns.detail: Thank them, confirm base/comp and role, ask for the benefits summary in writing with a date. Keeps momentum without locking blind.

columns.name: Hard accept / resign elsewhere
columns.detail: Wait for the benefits packet (or a written summary of the big four: health, 401k match, PTO, equity/bonus). Resigning on vibes is how people get surprised.

blocks.heading: Minimum written facts before a hard yes

items.label: Health plan type + employee premium estimate
items.detail: High-deductible vs PPO changes take-home a lot.

items.label: Retirement match formula
items.detail: Percent and vesting — not just 'we have a 401k'.

items.label: PTO / sick / holidays
items.detail: Especially if you are comparing against a current job.

items.label: Bonus / equity eligibility and timing
items.detail: Offer letter vs handbook — know which document wins.

blocks.title: A calm reply that buys the packet
blocks.body: I'm excited about the role and the base compensation. Before I give a final acceptance, could you send the benefits summary (medical premiums, 401k match, PTO, and any bonus/equity eligibility) by [date]? Happy to hop on a quick call if that is faster.

blocks.title: When waiting is not free
blocks.body: If the employer has a real exploding deadline, ask whether a conditional accept pending benefits review is allowed. If they refuse any written benefits detail, that itself is information.
